subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The charge difference across a resting neuron's membrane is the:
questions.explain: About -70 mV, maintained by the sodium–potassium pump.

questions.q: Depolarisation during an action potential is caused by:
options: Sodium ions rushing into the neuron
questions.explain: Voltage-gated Na+ channels open, reversing the membrane potential.

questions.q: Myelination speeds up impulses because the action potential:
options: Jumps between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction)
questions.explain: Leaping node to node greatly increases conduction speed.

questions.q: At a synapse, neurotransmitter is released when the presynaptic terminal:
options: Takes in calcium ions and vesicles fuse with the membrane
questions.explain: Ca2+ influx triggers exocytosis of neurotransmitter.

questions.q: The all-or-nothing principle means an action potential:
options: Fires fully at or above threshold, not at all below it
questions.explain: Stimulus strength is coded by frequency, not size.

questions.q: A neuron carrying impulses from receptors to the CNS is a:
questions.explain: Sensory (afferent) neurons carry impulses to the CNS.

questions.q: The two systems that coordinate the mammalian body are the:
questions.explain: Fast electrical and slower chemical signals integrate responses.

questions.q: The central nervous system consists of the:
questions.explain: The CNS integrates information.

questions.q: A reflex is rapid and involuntary because the signal:
options: Passes through the spinal cord without waiting for the brain
questions.explain: Reflex arcs route through the spinal cord for speed.

questions.q: Homeostasis relies on negative feedback, in which a change triggers responses that:
options: Reverse the change toward the set point
questions.explain: Negative feedback restores stable internal conditions.

questions.q: Blood glucose control by insulin and glucagon is an example of:
questions.explain: Antagonistic hormones keep glucose near a set point.

questions.q: A first-line, non-specific barrier to infection is the:
questions.explain: Physical/chemical barriers block pathogen entry.

questions.q: Phagocytes defend the body by:
questions.explain: Phagocytosis is part of innate immunity.

questions.q: Antibodies are produced by:
questions.explain: B cells and plasma cells make specific antibodies.

questions.q: An antibody binds a specific molecule on a pathogen called an:
questions.explain: Antibodies bind antigens, marking pathogens for destruction.

questions.q: Vaccination gives long-term protection mainly by producing:
questions.explain: Memory cells allow a rapid secondary response.

questions.q: Antibiotics work against bacteria but not viruses because they:
options: Target features of bacterial cells that viruses lack
questions.explain: Viruses use host cells and lack the bacterial targets.

questions.q: Overuse of antibiotics increases resistance because it:
options: Selects for pre-existing resistant bacteria that reproduce
questions.explain: This is natural selection acting on bacterial populations.

questions.q: Compared with hormonal control, nervous control is generally:
questions.explain: The two systems integrate rapid and sustained responses.

questions.q: Herd immunity protects unvaccinated people because:
questions.explain: With enough immune individuals the pathogen cannot spread easily.
